title: Common bile duct stones and acute cholangitis (India)

evidenceAudit.scope: Common bile duct (CBD) stones in adults in India, with obstructive jaundice, acute cholangitis or biliary pancreatitis: recognition, work-up, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) and surgical options, and antibiotics, built on the ICMR CBD Stone STW (July 2022) and NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025.
findings: When to suspect CBD stones, cholangitis features, investigations, magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) or endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) as the investigation of choice, ERCP as first line, surgical and stenting options, CBD closure options, and referral of palpable gallbladder with jaundice or grossly dilated CBD checked against the ICMR CBD Stone STW (July 2022).
Cholangitis antibiotics with and without sepsis (5–7 days after drainage) and the statement that biliary drainage is of utmost importance checked against NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 4.4.
unverifiedSections: The ICMR workflow gives no ERCP timing or cholangitis severity grading; Tokyo grading is not reproduced here.
Antibiotic doses are from NTG 2025 (cholecystitis and cholangitis section).
Paediatric CBD stones are outside the scope of the cited sources.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Stones in the common bile duct usually pass from the gallbladder and may block bile flow, causing obstructive jaundice. Bacteria then multiply in the stagnant, pressurised bile and enter the blood: acute cholangitis, with pain, fever with chills and jaundice, and in severe cases shock and confusion. Stones can also impact at the ampulla and trigger biliary pancreatitis. Diagnosis rests on deranged liver tests and a dilated duct on ultrasound, confirmed by MRCP or EUS. Treatment is resuscitation, antibiotics and, above all, biliary drainage, usually by ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone clearance, then cholecystectomy (ICMR STW; NTG 2025).
keyMechanisms: Gallstones migrate into the CBD and obstruct bile flow.
Raised biliary pressure drives bacteria and toxins into the blood (cholangiovenous reflux).
Ampullary impaction obstructs the pancreatic duct and causes pancreatitis.
Prolonged obstruction causes cholestatic liver injury and coagulopathy.

symptoms: Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain
Jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, itch
Pain radiating to back (biliary pancreatitis) (ICMR STW)
physicalSigns: Hypotension, confusion in severe cholangitis (shock) (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Shock with fever and jaundice: severe cholangitis needing urgent drainage (ICMR STW; NTG 2025)
Palpable gallbladder with jaundice: possible malignancy; refer (ICMR STW)
Grossly dilated CBD: possible choledochal cyst; refer (ICMR STW)
Raised amylase or lipase: biliary pancreatitis (ICMR STW)
precipitants: Previous cholecystectomy (retained or recurrent stones) (ICMR STW)
Biliary stricture or ampullary stenosis (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Painless progressive jaundice, weight loss, palpable gallbladder.
Very high transaminases; normal duct calibre.
Normal bilirubin and ALP; normal CBD.
Fever, tender liver, abscess on ultrasound.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Gallstone disease with deranged liver tests, dilated CBD on ultrasound, raised total leucocyte count or features of cholangitis.
Abdominal pain, fever with chills, with or without shock.
MRCP or EUS when ultrasound does not show CBD stones.

ruleIn.normalValue: Bilirubin below 1.2 mg/dL; ALP within range; INR about 1.0
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Raised bilirubin and ALP; prolonged INR
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Deranged LFT suggests CBD stones (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Resuscitate
actions: IV fluids, blood cultures, IV antibiotics (NTG 2025).
Shock or confusion: intensive care unit (ICU) and urgent drainage.

clinicalManagement.title: Biliary drainage
actions: Biliary drainage or relief of obstruction is of utmost importance (NTG 2025).
ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone clearance is first line, preferably at a tertiary centre (ICMR STW).
Large or difficult stones: endoscopic stenting then repeat ERCP and cholecystectomy (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Surgical options
actions: Laparoscopic or open cholecystectomy with CBD exploration (ICMR STW).
CBD closure: primary, T-tube, primary with endobiliary stent (remove within 6 weeks) or drainage procedure (ICMR STW).
Bypass (choledochoduodenostomy, hepaticojejunostomy) for multiple stones, hepatolithiasis, CBD over 2 cm or ampullary stricture (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Gallbladder
actions: Cholecystectomy after duct clearance; see Gallstone disease topic.

medicationPlan.note: Antibiotic regimens are from NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 4.4; the procedure pathway from the ICMR CBD Stone STW (2022). Drainage matters more than antibiotic choice. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: CBD stones and cholangitis in India.
learningObjectives: Suspect CBD stones from liver tests and ultrasound.
Arrange drainage and the right antibiotics.
keyPoints: Pain, fever with chills, jaundice: cholangitis.
ERCP first line; drainage is the key treatment.
pitfalls: Missing malignancy with painless jaundice and palpable gallbladder.
Forgetting to remove an endobiliary stent within 6 weeks.
